analysis: The overnight tape is AI-rally fatigue meeting a rates pushback. Versus the 4am brief, futures slid further to session lows (S&P -0.34%, Dow -0.58%, Nasdaq about -0.6% to -0.7%), the 30-year hit a fresh 24-year high (5.70%), and today's macro calendar crystallized: a $39B 10-year auction at 1pm ET (Cardillo: yield direction is the day's key driver) then Fed minutes at 2pm ET. Barron's trillion-dollar piece quantifies the concentration story: only 4 of 13 $1T stocks beat the S&P 500's 14.4% YTD, Bespoke flags six as overbought (Micron, AMD, Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla) and SpaceX as 'extremely overbought.' UBS's Haefele warning on narrowing breadth is now the consensus frame. On names: the SpaceX $40B FT financing scoop stays single-source headline risk (NVDA barely moving remains the tell); Intel/TSMC's Terafab partial reversal is holding; STZ's post-earnings slide is deepening (-5.6% to -8%) on soft Modelo/Corona demand; BNT (+15%) and TAP.A (+9.8%) lead premarket movers. Bank week starts Tuesday with Wall St H1 profits at $45.9B (NY Comptroller) setting a high bar. Community signal was nil: the HN thread on the SpaceX scoop has zero comments, and no qualifying Reddit threads surfaced. Nothing here changes the 4am setup; it sharpens it into a yields-and-breadth day.

headlines.headline: Futures hit session lows: Dow E-minis -0.58%, S&P 500 E-minis -0.34%, Nasdaq 100 futures about -0.6% to -0.7%. The 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.70%, a fresh 24-year high; the 10-year rose to 5.323-5.337%. Brent climbed 1.5% to $102.08 on Hormuz/Houthi escalation; WTI hovered near $90.
headlines.why_it_matters: Profit-taking after back-to-back records — the bond selloff and rebounding oil are doing the damage, and the slide coincided with the latest yield bump.

headlines.headline: Treasury auctions $39 billion of 10-year notes at 1pm ET today. Spartan Capital's Peter Cardillo says the auction result will gauge fixed-income sentiment and 'thus stocks' — yield direction is the day's key driving force.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh supply into a 24-year-high long end — a weak auction pushes yields higher and tightens the squeeze on the record tape.

headlines.headline: Only four of the 13 trillion-dollar stocks are beating the S&P 500 (+14.4% YTD): Nvidia +30% (nearing a $6T market cap), Apple +23% (~$4.9T), Meta +12.7% (Muse AI agent boost); Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft each +10-11%; Tesla -15%. Bespoke flags six as overbought (Micron, AMD, Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla) and SpaceX as 'extremely overbought.'
headlines.why_it_matters: Quantifies the narrowing-breadth warning — the AI rally is concentrated in names now flagged as technically stretched.

headlines.headline: Brookfield Wealth Solutions (BNT) led premarket movers, up 15.0% about two hours before the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Standout premarket mover — the stock-specific story is doing the work against a soft tape.

headlines.headline: Molson Coors Beverage Cl A (TAP.A) rose 9.8% in premarket trading, among the top S&P 500 premarket gainers.
headlines.why_it_matters: Defensive/staple strength on a risk-off morning — a rotation cue while megacap futures fade.

headlines.headline: Constellation Brands (STZ) slide deepening to -5.6% to -8% premarket after beating Q2 targets but signaling weak underlying demand for Modelo Especial and Corona Extra.
headlines.why_it_matters: Beat-but-soft-guide is getting punished harder than the 4am print suggested — revenue quality, not the headline beat, sets the open.

headlines.headline: SpaceX (SPCX) fell 2.1% premarket after the Financial Times reported the company is seeking $40 billion in financing (Apollo-led) to fund purchases of Nvidia chips; Nvidia barely moved (-0.2%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Financing overhang on the newest trillion-dollar name — but single-source, unconfirmed: no SpaceX or Nvidia confirmation, so treat as fragile; NVDA barely moving is the tell that no confirmed demand event exists yet.
